title: Episode 162: Sean Parent on the History of Pascal

sentences.en: C was never a particularly elegant language.
sentences.zh: C 语言从来就不是一门特别优雅的语言。

sentences.en: Pascal, by comparison, is a very elegant language.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，Pascal 是一门非常优雅的语言。

sentences.en: C was always difficult to parse compared to Pascal.
sentences.zh: 跟 Pascal 相比，C 语言一直很难解析。

sentences.en: So there were a lot of things working against it.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有很多因素对它不利。

sentences.en: But one of the things working for it is C from the get-go tended to have direct compilers targeting the assembly language of whatever machine you were working on,
sentences.zh: 但对它有利的一点是，C 语言从一开始就倾向于拥有直接针对你所使用的任何机器的汇编语言的编译器，

sentences.en: where Pascal still, for the most part, relied on P code with a few exceptions.
sentences.zh: 而 Pascal 在大多数情况下仍然依赖于 P 码，只有少数例外。

sentences.en: Apple had a compiler to 68K, but almost everybody else was running through P code.
sentences.zh: 苹果有一个针对 68K 的编译器，但几乎其他所有人都在通过 P 码运行。

sentences.en: And so Pascal was viewed as being slow and interpreted.
sentences.zh: 因此，Pascal 被视为运行缓慢且经过解释的语言。

sentences.en: And the whole object Pascal thing was viewed as being Apple's extension.
sentences.zh: 而且整个对象 Pascal 被视为苹果的扩展。

sentences.en: And so it did not get wide use outside of the Apple ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 因此它在苹果生态系统之外并没有得到广泛使用。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 162, recorded on December 12, 2023.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看 ADSP 播客第 162 期，录制于 2023 年 12 月 12 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳。

sentences.en: And today with my co-host, Bryce, we continue our conversation with Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 今天，我和我的联合主持人布莱伊斯将继续与肖恩·帕伦特的对话。

sentences.en: And in this episode, chat with him about the history of Pascal, Pascal versus C, other Nicholas Wirth programming languages, and more.
sentences.zh: 在这一期节目中，我们与他聊了聊 Pascal 的历史、Pascal 与 C 的对比、尼克劳斯·维尔特的其它编程语言等等。

sentences.en: We've now skipped ahead over Zach.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经跳过了扎克。

sentences.zh: 节日快乐。

sentences.zh: 我想这应该正好在元旦之前。

sentences.zh: 你怎么称呼那个？

sentences.en: With respect to the, what are we, Julian Gregorian calendar?
sentences.zh: 关于那个，我们用的是什么历法，儒略历还是格里高利历？

sentences.en: One of the two.
sentences.zh: 两者之一。

sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以如果你现在正在听这个，祝你新年快乐或者除夕快乐。

sentences.zh: 我们请肖恩回来的最初原因——我们会在本期节目Shownotes的最上方贴出链接——

sentences.en: is we did a series of conversations with Jonathan O'Connor where we were talking about a plethora of stuff,
sentences.zh: 是我们之前和乔纳森·奥康纳做了一系列对话，聊了各种各样的事情，

sentences.en: but a couple of the episodes focused on Pascal versus Ada versus C, and there was a bunch of stuff that we chatted about.
sentences.zh: 但其中几期节目重点聊了 Pascal、Ada 和 C 的对比，我们聊了很多内容。

sentences.en: But, Sean, you ended up replying to, I believe it was the tweet on episode 154, which was, I think, like part two or part three of that talk.
sentences.zh: 但是，肖恩，你最终回复了，我记得那是针对第 154 期的推文，那好像是那次访谈的第二部分或第三部分。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to read out everything because it was about three or four tweets in a row.
sentences.zh: 我不会把所有内容都读出来，因为它大概连续发了三四条推文。

sentences.en: But you mentioned a bunch of stuff that didn't get mentioned in that conversation.
sentences.zh: 但你提到了很多在那次对话中没有被提及的事情。

sentences.en: You know, if I peruse through this tweet, it's mentioning the Apple Lisa and macOS were written in a combination of Pascal and 68K.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果我浏览一下这条推文，它提到苹果 Lisa 和 macOS 是用 Pascal 和 68K 的组合编写的。

sentences.en: And then you mentioned a bunch of different books, a bunch of different computers.
sentences.zh: 然后你提到了许多不同的书籍、许多不同的计算机。

sentences.en: And I'll probably just leave it there and just throw it over to you.
sentences.zh: 我可能就说到这里，然后把话筒交给你。

sentences.en: And you can start wherever you want to start with, you know, the things that we missed and that you were sort of, you know, screaming in your head.
sentences.zh: 你可以从你想要开始的地方开始，讲讲那些我们漏掉的、而你当时在脑海里直呼的事情，

sentences.en: How come they're not mentioning this?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么不提这个？

sentences.en: How come they're not mentioning this?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么不提这个？

sentences.en: And that's what the next, you know, either part two or part three or maybe doing one part of this conversation will be.
sentences.zh: 这就是接下来的部分，无论是第二部分、第三部分，还是把这次对话分成一部分的内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, so a combination of that.
sentences.zh: 对，所以是这些因素的结合。

sentences.en: And then I was listening to Software Unscripted, and you made a guest appearance there, Connor, on that podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我当时在听《Software Unscripted》，康纳，你作为嘉宾上了那一期播客。

sentences.en: And you mentioned that you were born, I think, in 1990, if that's correct.
sentences.zh: 你提到你出生于 1990 年左右，如果我没记错的话。

sentences.en: That is correct, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, which just made me feel very old.
sentences.zh: 对，对，这让我觉得自己非常老。

sentences.en: I joined Apple three years before you were born.
sentences.zh: 在你出生前三年我就加入苹果了。

sentences.en: I mean, I was, we were interviewing on my other podcast at Raycast, Brian Ellingsgaard, who is 18, which means that he was born in 2005.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们在我的另一个播客 Raycast 上采访了布赖恩·埃林斯高，他 18 岁，这意味着他出生于 2005 年。

sentences.en: So, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的。

sentences.en: Oh, I don't, there's, I didn't, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不知道，没有，我没有……

sentences.en: People shouldn't be that, yeah.
sentences.zh: 人们不应该那么……对。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: So, like, I didn't know how young he was.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道他这么年轻。

sentences.en: And then when he said he was 18, I was like, oh, God, that may, so if you're feeling old about me and I'm feeling old about Brian, you know, it's just this vicious,
sentences.zh: 然后当他说他 18 岁时，我想，天哪，所以如果你因为我而觉得自己老，而我又因为布赖恩而觉得自己老，你知道，这就是一个恶性循环，

sentences.en: vicious feedback loop here.
sentences.zh: 一个恶性的反馈回路。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And, like, like, not knowing, kind of, you know, Pascal and that history was interesting.
sentences.zh: 而且，某种程度上，不了解 Pascal 及其历史是很有意思的。

sentences.en: Pascal had a, had a, had a pretty significant heyday.
sentences.zh: Pascal 曾有过一段相当辉煌的全盛时期。

sentences.en: And even going all the way back to the Apple II, there was an implementation of UCSD Pascal, which if you wanted to, you know, program, you know, a 68K processor,
sentences.zh: 甚至一直追溯到 Apple II，当时有一个 UCSD Pascal 的实现版本，如果你想给……编程的话，

sentences.en: which was the old Apple II, was a, a, an 8-bit processor.
sentences.zh: 也就是老旧的 Apple II 搭载的是一个 8 位处理器。

sentences.en: So, even doing, you know, 16-bit arithmetic was a challenge.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使是进行 16 位算术运算也是一个挑战。

sentences.en: Steve Wozniak wrote something called Sweet 16, which was kind of a, a, a pseudo 16-bit assembly language that executed in, in 6502 as a, as a way to,
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克写了一个叫作 Sweet 16 的东西，它有点像一个伪 16 位汇编语言，在 6502 中执行，作为一种方法，

sentences.en: to write 16-bit assembly language easier.
sentences.zh: 以便更轻松地编写 16 位汇编语言。

sentences.en: So, Pascal had a bit of a heyday at that time.
sentences.zh: 所以 Pascal 在当时确实有过一段全盛时期。

sentences.en: And there was an implementation from University of California, San Diego, UCSD.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个来自加州大学圣迭戈分校（UCSD）的实现版本。

sentences.en: That's, that's what I was thinking that UCSD stood for, but I was like, that can't be, I must be, there must be some other acronym, and that's the only one I know,
sentences.zh: 这就是我当时想的 UCSD 代表的意思，但我在想，这不对吧，我肯定记错了，肯定还有别的缩写，而这是我唯一知道的，

sentences.en: so that's what I'm thinking of.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想的就是这个。

sentences.en: But that's, it is what it stood for.
sentences.zh: 但它确实就是这个意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, so, so an implementation came out of there.
sentences.zh: 对，所以一个实现版本就是从那里出来的。

sentences.en: And, and it was based off of something called P-code, where P-code is basically a, a, a byte code that's easily interpreted.
sentences.zh: 它基于一种叫作 P 码的东西，P 码基本上是一种易于解释的字节码。

sentences.en: And so the idea with UCSD Pascal was, you could, it was kind of, you know, pre-Java, Java, it was, you could compile your Pascal code down to P-code,
sentences.zh: 所以 UCSD Pascal 的理念是——这有点像是前 Java 时代的 Java——你可以把你的 Pascal 代码编译成 P 码，

sentences.en: and then you could run that P-code any place that had a P-code interpreter, and building a P-code interpreter was dead simple.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以在任何拥有 P 码解释器的地方运行该 P 码，并且构建一个 P 码解释器极其简单。

sentences.en: So it meant that you could write, write Pascal code, and have it run basically anywhere.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可以编写 Pascal 代码，并基本上让它在任何地方运行。

sentences.en: So Pascal itself became kind of the moral equivalent to what we would now think of as, as, as Python, which is kind of an application language.
sentences.zh: 因此，Pascal 本身在某种程度上成了我们现在所认为的 Python 的精神等价物，它有点像是一种应用语言。

sentences.en: If you needed to, to, to write software, and you weren't, you know, to solve a problem, right, using, using a programming language as an app, right,
sentences.zh: 如果你需要编写软件，而不是为了解决问题——对吧，使用编程语言作为一个应用，对吧——

sentences.en: so you're writing software to solve a problem, as opposed to building a product.
sentences.zh: 所以你编写软件是为了解决问题，而不是为了构建产品。

sentences.en: Pascal got, got an awful lot, lot of use in, in that environment.
sentences.zh: Pascal 在那种环境中得到了大量的应用。

sentences.en: And it also became a, a, a great teaching language, and then, uh, uh, it started to bleed into system languages.
sentences.zh: 它也成了一门极佳的教学语言，然后，它开始渗透到系统语言中。

sentences.en: So the, the original, uh, Lisa, uh, was written, the operating system itself was written in a combination of Pascal, uh, compiled to, to 68,000, and, uh, 68K assembly language.
sentences.zh: 所以，最初的 Lisa 操作系统本身是用 Pascal（编译为 68000 汇编语言）和 68K 汇编语言的组合编写的。

sentences.en: And then, uh, uh, and then, uh, Larry Tesler, who had come out of Xerox PARC, worked with Nicholas Wirt, who, who created Pascal, uh, to define object Pascal.
sentences.zh: 然后，从施乐帕克（Xerox PARC）出来的拉里·泰斯勒与创建了 Pascal 的尼克劳斯·维尔特合作，共同定义了对象 Pascal。

sentences.en: And that kind of became the, the language of choice for writing applications on the, on the Lisa.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上成了在 Lisa 上编写应用程序的首选语言。

sentences.en: And that same basic model moved into the early Macintosh.
sentences.zh: 而同样的基本模型也被带到了早期的 Macintosh 中。

sentences.en: So the initial Macintosh, the operating system was written in a combination of 68K assembly language and Pascal,
sentences.zh: 因此，最初的 Macintosh，其操作系统是用 68K 汇编语言和 Pascal 的组合编写的，

sentences.en: and then most applications written on top of the early Macintoshes were written in object Pascal.
sentences.zh: 然后早期 Macintosh 上编写的大多数应用程序都是用对象 Pascal 编写的。

sentences.en: You know, object Pascal eventually morphed into, into Delphi.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，对象 Pascal 最终演变成了 Delphi。

sentences.en: So that's, there's a, there's a direct lineage there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里面有着直接的传承关系。

sentences.en: But what happened was Unix took root in universities and kind of displaced, uh, uh, many computer operating systems like VaxVMS got eventually displaced with Unix distributions.
sentences.zh: 但发生的情况是，Unix 在大学里扎根，并逐渐取代了许多计算机操作系统，比如 VaxVMS 最终被 Unix 发行版所取代。

sentences.en: And Unix was very much built around, uh, the C language.
sentences.zh: 而 Unix 很大程度上是围绕着 C 语言构建的。

sentences.en: And so C started getting taught, um, uh, uh, in universities and displaced Pascal as a language of choice for, for a teaching language.
sentences.zh: 因此，C 语言开始在大学里被教授，并取代 Pascal 成为首选的教学语言。

sentences.en: And there became this large ecosystem of developer tooling, uh, built in C.
sentences.zh: 并且出现了一个用 C 语言构建的庞大开发者工具生态系统。

sentences.en: And so there became all these external pressures to, to move towards C.
sentences.zh: 因此，出现了转向 C 语言的各种外部压力。

sentences.en: So eventually in, you know, kind of early nineties timeframe, Apple transitioned, uh, Mac development from, from Pascal to, to C.
sentences.zh: 所以最终在 90 年代初左右，苹果将 Mac 的开发从 Pascal 过渡到了 C 语言。

sentences.en: And Photoshop was originally written in, in, in, in object Pascal in 1990.
sentences.zh: Photoshop 最初是在 1990 年用对象 Pascal 编写的。

sentences.en: And let's see, probably around 92, I would guess, uh, Photoshop was ported from object Pascal to C plus plus.
sentences.zh: 让我想想，大概在 92 年左右吧我猜，Photoshop 从对象 Pascal 被移植到了 C++。

sentences.en: And that was back in C front days where it was, you know, Bjarne's compiler that compiled C plus plus code into C and then you compile a C code into your, your machine code.
sentences.zh: 那是 Cfront 时代，那是本贾尼的编译器，它将 C++ 代码编译成 C，然后你再将 C 代码编译成机器码。

sentences.en: And wait, so, so you said that this shift was just happening because Unix was gaining popularity and Unix was associated with C.
sentences.zh: 等等，所以你说这种转变之所以发生，只是因为 Unix 越来越受欢迎，而 Unix 与 C 语言息息相关。

sentences.en: So, and, and you mentioned that C started to get taught in universities because of this, but at the same time,
sentences.zh: 所以，你提到 C 语言因此开始在大学里被教授，但与此同时，

sentences.en: Pascal and object Pascal or versions of Pascal were also being taught.
sentences.zh: Pascal、对象 Pascal 或 Pascal 的各种版本也同样在被教授。

sentences.en: So it was just momentum that like Unix and C had more momentum than the, the family of Pascal languages.
sentences.zh: 所以这纯粹是势头问题，Unix 和 C 语言比 Pascal 语言家族拥有更强的势头。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was, it was largely just momentum.
sentences.zh: 对，这在很大程度上只是势头问题。

sentences.en: It got to the point where, you know, it was like, well, I could write this in Pascal, but look, there's all these, these tools that do this in C and you start hiring people.
sentences.zh: 发展到一定程度，你知道的，就像是，‘好吧，我可以用 Pascal 编写这个，但是看，有这么多用 C 语言做这件事的工具’，然后你开始招聘人员。

sentences.en: And it became hard to hire somebody who knew Pascal, they knew C.
sentences.zh: 招聘一个懂 Pascal 的人变得很困难，大家都懂 C。

sentences.en: So there was this momentum shift and, and from kind of, you know, building an operating system.
sentences.zh: 因此产生了一种势头的转变，从构建操作系统的角度来看。

sentences.en: There were certain things that were, you know, a little bit easier to express in C, right?
sentences.zh: 有些事情在 C 语言中表达起来稍微容易一些，对吧？

sentences.en: It was just easier to circumvent the type system and kind of do whatever you wanted.
sentences.zh: 绕过类型系统并随心所欲地做你想做的事要容易得多。

sentences.en: Although, you know, in Pascal, Apple would do that by just dropping into 68K assembly language and, and, and writing little snippets like that where, where C was not sufficient.
sentences.zh: 尽管，你知道的，在 Pascal 中，苹果可以通过直接转入 68K 汇编语言并编写诸如此类的小代码片段来做到这一点，在 C 语言不够用的时候。

sentences.en: But, you know, for a while there, it was very unclear that C was never a particularly elegant language.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，有那么一段时间，很不确定，C 语言从来都不是一门特别优雅的语言。

sentences.en: That's just, Pascal, by comparison, is, is a very elegant language.
sentences.zh: 这就是，相比之下，Pascal 是一门非常优雅的语言。

sentences.en: C was always difficult to parse compared to Pascal.
sentences.zh: 跟 Pascal 相比，C 语言一直很难解析。

sentences.en: So there were, there were a lot of things working against it.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有很多因素对它不利。

sentences.en: But one of the things working for it is C from the get go tended to have direct compilers targeting the assembly language of whatever machine you were working on,
sentences.zh: 但对它有利的一点是，C 语言从一开始就倾向于拥有直接针对你所使用的任何机器的汇编语言的编译器，

sentences.en: where Pascal still, for the most part, relied on, on P code with, you know, a few exceptions.
sentences.zh: 而 Pascal 在大多数情况下仍然依赖于 P 码，只有少数例外。

sentences.en: Apple had a compiler to 68K, but almost everybody else was running through P code.
sentences.zh: 苹果有一个针对 68K 的编译器，但几乎其他所有人都在通过 P 码运行。

sentences.en: And so Pascal was viewed as being slow and interpreted.
sentences.zh: 因此，Pascal 被视为运行缓慢且经过解释的语言。

sentences.en: And the whole object Pascal thing was viewed as being Apple's, Apple's extension.
sentences.zh: 而且整个对象 Pascal 被视为苹果的扩展。

sentences.en: And so it was not, did not get wide use outside of the Apple ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 因此它在苹果生态系统之外并没有得到广泛使用。

sentences.en: You know, talking about P code reminds me that, and this is, this is going to be embarrassing for Connor and I.
sentences.zh: 说到 P 码，这让我想起了一件事，这对康纳和我来说会有点尴尬。

sentences.en: During our previous discussion, Connor, I don't think we talked about the fact that I'm pretty certain that the book ADSP, algorithms plus data structures equals programs,
sentences.zh: 在我们之前的讨论中，康纳，我觉得我们没有讨论过这样一件事：我非常确信那本书——ADSP，即《算法 + 数据结构 = 程序》——

sentences.en: is largely in Pascal.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是用 Pascal 写的。

sentences.en: And in fact, I, I, I, I believe that my original encounter with P code was that there's a, like a, they,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我相信我最初接触 P 码是因为书里有一个，就像是，他们

sentences.en: they write like a little Pascal compiler in the book with a very slimmed down version of the VM.
sentences.zh: 在书中用一个精简版的虚拟机编写了一个小型的 Pascal 编译器。

sentences.en: And I only just now remember, so clearly neither of us have read the book that recently.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚才想起来，显然我们俩最近都没有读过这本书。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it, because of the conversation with Jonathan, I did go out immediately after recording that I bought a hard copy book and it's sitting on my shelf now.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是说，因为和乔纳森的对话，录制结束后我确实立刻出去买了一本实体书，它现在正放在我的书架上。

sentences.en: And because it was, it was when he said that, yes, it's considered like a teaching book for Pascal.
sentences.zh: 因为当他说出那句话时，是的，它被认为是一本 Pascal 的教材。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, that's, you know, clearly we haven't read it, but like, we didn't even know the basics of what I thought this book was like a generic,
sentences.zh: 我当时想，哦，你知道的，显然我们没读过它，但我们甚至不知道这本书的基础知识，我还以为它是一本通用的、

sentences.en: just kind of data structures and algorithms book.
sentences.zh: 只是关于数据结构和算法的书呢。

sentences.en: But, but yes.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的。

sentences.en: So at some point we will read it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在某个时候会去读它。

sentences.en: I did not know that about the P code though.
sentences.zh: 不过关于 P 码我确实不知道这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think, I think, cause I, I, I seem to recall that like the Turbo Pascal compiler was like inspired by the, the little teaching compiler.
sentences.zh: 我想，因为我隐约记得 Turbo Pascal 编译器似乎是受到 ADSP 书中那个小型教学编译器的启发。

sentences.en: That was in the ADSP book.
sentences.zh: 就是那本 ADSP 书里的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There was, uh, Turbo Pascal first appeared on, well, I was going to say windows, but DOS I think would be correct.
sentences.zh: 当时，Turbo Pascal 首先出现在——嗯，我本想说 Windows，但 DOS 应该更准确。

sentences.en: Uh, so on Microsoft platform and yeah, Turbo Pascal was just an amazing, you know, little IDE and compiler that was just blazing fast and, and it was not P code based,
sentences.zh: 所以是在微软平台上，是的，Turbo Pascal 只是一个令人惊叹的小型 IDE 和编译器，速度极快，而且它不是基于 P 码的，

sentences.en: went straight to, uh, uh, 68 K assembly.
sentences.zh: 直接生成 68K 汇编代码。

sentences.en: Um, Apple in the early Mac days, they had an, they had their, their Apple compiler, but they also had something called Apple Pascal, which was the same name as,
sentences.zh: 苹果在早期 Mac 时代，他们有自己的苹果编译器，但他们也有一个叫作 Apple Pascal 的东西，这个名字和

sentences.en: as the Pascal that Apple had on Apple too.
sentences.zh: 苹果在 Apple II 上拥有的 Pascal 名字相同。

sentences.en: But Apple Pascal on a Mac was an interpreted Pascal that was very much centered around kind of, you know, programming as, as an application, right.
sentences.zh: 但 Mac 上的 Apple Pascal 是一个经过解释的 Pascal，它在很大程度上以编写应用程序为核心，对吧。

sentences.en: As opposed to, to programming an application.
sentences.zh: 而不是编写一个应用程序。

sentences.en: So, so same way you would use, use Python today, right.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像你今天使用 Python 的方式一样，对吧。

sentences.en: You just want to want to solve a problem.
sentences.zh: 你只是想解决一个问题。

sentences.en: And it was, was, you know, very slick environment and debugging environment, uh, very easy to use, um, uh, very limited.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常流畅的环境和调试环境，非常易于使用，而且非常受限。

sentences.en: I think in your talk, somebody said like you could only have one file for a Pascal program.
sentences.zh: 我想在你的谈话中，有人说过一个 Pascal 程序只能有一个文件。

sentences.en: Uh, uh, not true, but that was true in, in, in Apple Pascal.
sentences.zh: 这并不属实，但在 Apple Pascal 中确实如此。

sentences.en: Um, uh, uh, and that file itself could only be 32 K in size.
sentences.zh: 而且该文件本身的大小只能有 32K。

sentences.en: And, uh, uh, I actually wrote a school project in, uh, in Pascal and ended up writing another tool in compiled Pascal that would process my, my Pascal, uh, to minify it.
sentences.zh: 我实际上用 Pascal 写过一个学校项目，最后用编译后的 Pascal 写了另一个工具来处理我的 Pascal 代码以对其进行代码压缩（minify）。

sentences.en: So that, cause I had to turn in the school project in Apple Pascal and so that I could fit more in, in the 32 K.
sentences.zh: 因为我必须用 Apple Pascal 提交学校项目，为了能把更多内容塞进 32K 里。

sentences.en: And so I turned in two listings.
sentences.zh: 所以我提交了两个代码清单。

sentences.en: One was the unminified code.
sentences.zh: 一个是未压缩的代码。

sentences.en: And then one was the code that actually ran, which was, was, was greatly reduced.
sentences.zh: 另一个是实际运行的代码，经过了大幅缩减。

sentences.en: And probably a lot less readable.
sentences.zh: 而且可读性要差得多。

sentences.en: And a lot less readable.
sentences.zh: 可读性差得多。

sentences.en: Also included, there was an escape patch.
sentences.zh: 其中还包含了一个逃逸补丁（escape patch）。

sentences.en: So you could execute assembly language.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以执行汇编语言。

sentences.en: And so there were sections of code where I just hand wrote them in assembly language and escaped from Pascal to assembly language.
sentences.zh: 所以有些代码段，我是直接用汇编语言手写的，从 Pascal 转到了汇编语言。

sentences.en: So, so, so not completely legit, but you know, it was, it was interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，虽然不是完全正统，但你知道，它挺有意思的。

sentences.en: I think a lot of ideas from Apple Pascal then, uh, got carried over into, uh, uh, and Turbo Pascal into ThinkC and then into, into, into MetroWorks, uh, Code Warrior.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当年 Apple Pascal 的很多理念，呃，后来传承到了，呃，呃，还有 Turbo Pascal，再到 ThinkC，然后又到了 MetroWorks 的，呃，Code Warrior。

sentences.en: Uh, I think the other thing that damaged Pascal was, Nicholas Wirt didn't, you know, he did Pascal and then he did Object Pascal.
sentences.zh: 呃，我觉得毁了 Pascal 的另一件事是，尼古拉斯·维尔特（Niklaus Wirth）没有，你知道，他先做了 Pascal，然后又做了对象 Pascal（Object Pascal）。

sentences.en: And then from what he learned from Object Pascal, he created Modula 2, or, well, first Modula and then Modula 2.
sentences.zh: 然后根据他从对象 Pascal 中学到的东西，他创造了 Modula 2，或者说，嗯，先是 Modula，然后是 Modula 2。

sentences.en: And then, then created Oberon.
sentences.zh: 接着，又创造了 Oberon。

sentences.en: And so, you know, he was a university guy.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他是个学院派。

sentences.en: And so he was kind of creating this stream of, of little languages and so abandoning his, his previous work.
sentences.zh: 因此他一直在创造这一系列的小众语言，从而不断抛弃他之前的工作。

sentences.en: And so I think that ended up damaging things, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这最终把事情搞砸了，对吧？

sentences.en: There got to be the point where, you know, I, I did work, actually shipped a product that was partially written in Modula 2, uh, before MetroWorks did Code Warrior.
sentences.zh: 到了某个阶段，你知道，我确实做过一些工作，实际上发布过一个部分用 Modula 2 编写的产品，是在 MetroWorks 做出 Code Warrior 之前。

sentences.en: Greg Galanos wrote, uh, Modula 2 compiler for Mac.
sentences.zh: 格雷格·加拉诺斯（Greg Galanos）为 Mac 编写过，呃，Modula 2 编译器。

sentences.en: I probably still have someplace here, my, uh, my Modula 2 book.
sentences.zh: 我大概还在什么地方留着我的，呃，我的 Modula 2 书。

sentences.en: People were doing, well, is it going to be Modula 2 next?
sentences.zh: 当时大家都在想，嗯，接下来会是 Modula 2 吗？

sentences.en: Is it going to be, you know, are we doing Modula 2?
sentences.zh: 会是，你知道的，我们在搞 Modula 2 吗？

sentences.en: Are we doing Object Pascal?
sentences.zh: 我们在搞对象 Pascal 吗？

sentences.en: Oh, wait, now we're doing Oberon.
sentences.zh: 哦，等等，现在我们在搞 Oberon。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And so, so just that lineage kind of confused the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 所以，正是这种血统把市场给搞糊涂了。

sentences.en: And, and C++ had this much more straightforward story.
sentences.zh: 而且，C++ 的发展脉络要清晰得多。

sentences.en: That is, uh, it's incredibly reminiscent of what, I mean, I've told this story a couple times on the podcast of what Arthur Whitney has done with, uh,
sentences.zh: 这真是，呃，极其让人想起——我是说，我在播客里提过好几次这个故事——亚瑟·惠特尼（Arthur Whitney）用，呃，

sentences.en: all the different K languages that he's written.
sentences.zh: 他编写的所有那些不同的 K 语言所做的事情。

sentences.en: That he'll finish with one, even more aggressively will delete it, clear all of, you know, the remnants of it off his workstation or laptop and then move on to the next thing.
sentences.zh: 他用完一种语言后，甚至会更加激进地将它删除，把工作站或笔记本电脑上所有，你知道的，关于它的残余痕迹清得干干净净，然后就转向下一个东西。

sentences.en: And, and yeah, like there's definitely that same kind of effect on the community that's using it.
sentences.zh: 而且，没错，对使用它的社区来说，绝对也有那种类似的影响。

sentences.en: You know, people, is K6 going to be the final one?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大家都在想，K6 会是最后一个吗？

sentences.en: Is K7, is there going to be another one?
sentences.zh: K7 呢，还会有别的吗？

sentences.en: And I think every, every time that a new one is created, people are more and more cautious to like move to the next one or do we just keep using what we have?
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得每次推出新语言时，大家在决定要不要转向新语言，或者是不是继续用手头现有的东西时，都会变得越来越谨慎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I wonder, cause the next name that comes to mind is on our Andrew Hausberg out of Microsoft, but he's almost the opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 我在想，因为脑海中浮现的下一个名字是微软的安德鲁·黑尔斯伯格（Andrew Hejlsberg），但他几乎完全相反。

sentences.en: Has worked on a ton of different, like majorly successful languages, but has not, it hasn't been like, you know, they, he, he made sure that the community was going to, you know,
sentences.zh: 他参与过大量不同的、可以说是极其成功的语言，但并没有——他确保了社区会，你知道的，

sentences.en: survive and continue to thrive.
sentences.zh: 能够生存并继续繁荣发展。

sentences.en: And then just moved on to the next project, uh, which I guess is, uh, you know, for any aspiring programming language creators do what Hausberg did and not what, not what, uh,
sentences.zh: 然后才转向下一个项目，呃，我想这对于任何有志于创建编程语言的人来说，应该去学黑尔斯伯格，而不是去学，而不是去学，呃，

sentences.en: Verth did or, or Whitney, or maybe there were, maybe, you know, Whitney's working towards, uh, a final one language to rule them all.
sentences.zh: 维尔特（Wirth），或者惠特尼，或者也许，你知道的，惠特尼正在朝着一种“一统江湖”的终极语言努力。

sentences.en: In which case, uh, there'll be a bit of an excitement around that, but I had no idea that that was kind of the reputation around, uh, what Verth was doing.
sentences.zh: 如果是那样的话，呃，大家可能会为此有点兴奋，但我真不知道维尔特当年干的事在名声上是这样的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I've often thought if you take a compiler class in school, you basically learn the dragon book and which is a great book,
sentences.zh: 我经常想，如果你在学校里上过编译器课程，你基本上学的就是《龙书》，那是一本极好的书，

sentences.en: but unless you're going to end up building compilers out of school, which very few people will, I think it's,
sentences.zh: 但除非你毕业后真的去开发编译器——极少数人会这么做——否则我认为，

sentences.en: it's overkill and, and Nicholas Verth's languages and, and his, his compiler, uh, books, uh, are much simpler the, the, the way Nicholas Verth always built a language.
sentences.zh: 这有点大材小用。而尼古拉斯·维尔特的语言和他的编译器，呃，书籍，要简单得多，尼古拉斯·维尔特构建语言的方式一直都是如此。

sentences.en: I call it LL one to the bottom, which is he would define an LL one grammar, which is, you know, a very simple recursive descent grammar with no backtracking.
sentences.zh: 我称之为自底向上的 LL(1)，也就是他会定义一个 LL(1) 文法，你知道的，这是一种非常简单的、没有回溯的递归下降文法。

sentences.en: If you, if you, if you, you know, if you don't get success on the next token, then your, your code is wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果你，如果你，如果你，你知道的，如果你在下一个记号（token）上没能匹配成功，那么你的代码就是错的。

sentences.en: And his compilers all generated code straight from the parser.
sentences.zh: 他的编译器全都是直接从语法分析器（parser）生成代码。

sentences.en: He never built an ASt.
sentences.zh: 他从不构建抽象语法树（AST）。

sentences.en: Uh, so he would compile straight from, uh, straight from the parser into P code or, or, or into assembly language.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以他会直接从，呃，直接从解析器编译成 P 代码，或者，或者直接编译成汇编语言。

sentences.en: And so it's, it's a much simpler approach if you're, if you want to build, uh, a quick compiler one-off.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想快速搞出一个一次性的编译器，这是一种简单得多的方法。

sentences.en: Uh, it's really easy to build a little stack machine interpreter and then build a compiler that's recursive descent.
sentences.zh: 呃，构建一个小型的栈虚拟机解释器，然后再构建一个递归下降的编译器，真的非常容易。

sentences.en: And you just generate the code for your own stack machine straight out of your parser and you don't deal with ASTs and you don't, don't deal with extra complexity.
sentences.zh: 你直接从解析器里为自己的栈虚拟机生成代码，完全不用去处理 AST，也不用去应付额外的复杂性。

sentences.en: But is, is, um, is a Lisp really that was like, it's scheme and S in, in the, the dragon book, right?
sentences.zh: 不过，呃，Lisp 真的就是那样吗？《龙书》里讲的是 Scheme 和 S-表达式，对吧？

sentences.en: Uh, yeah, I believe it is scheme in the dragon book.
sentences.zh: 呃，对，我相信《龙书》里讲的就是 Scheme。

sentences.en: Is it really that much harder to, I mean, I, I do think they build an AST, but in that book, but is it really that much harder to parse?
sentences.zh: 解析起来真的有那么难吗？我是说，我的确觉得他们在书中构建了 AST，但解析真的有那么难吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no, it's not the, the, the, the, the parser in that language is, is that much simpler.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，倒不是说那个语言的解析器有多复杂。

sentences.en: It's just that they go through like all the steps of building a compiler and it's like you build your AST and then you do passes on it.
sentences.zh: 关键是他们走完了构建编译器的所有步骤，比如你得构建 AST，然后再对它进行各种遍历优化。

sentences.en: You're optimizers and you look, the dragon book is a thick book and nobody makes it through the dragon book in a quarter.
sentences.zh: 你看，《龙书》是一本很厚书，没人能在短短一个学期里啃完《龙书》。

sentences.en: I mean, come on, you're not, you're not actually doing that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，拜托，你根本不可能真的做到。

sentences.en: Uh, where I can't remember the name for, or for a Virat's book, but it's, it's a small, small book.
sentences.zh: 呃，虽然我记不清维尔特那本书的名字了，但它是一本很小很小的书。

sentences.en: Uh, and if you look like, you know, Nicholas Virat built, I think I mentioned it on Twitter, um, a machine called the Lilith, which was basically a Modula 2 machine.
sentences.zh: 呃，如果你看看，你知道的，尼古拉斯·维尔特——我想我在推特上提到过——曾制造过一台名为 Lilith 的机器，它基本上就是一台 Modula 2 机器。

sentences.en: What do you mean by he built a machine?
sentences.zh: 你说的“他制造了一台机器”是什么意思？

sentences.en: Uh, I mean, they were manufacturing and you could order a Lilith and, you know, like you could order an Apple II, you could order a Lilith.
sentences.zh: 呃，我的意思是，它们当时在量产，你可以订购一台 Lilith，你知道的，就像你可以订购一台 Apple II 一样，你可以订购一台 Lilith。

sentences.en: It was an expensive machine.
sentences.zh: 那是一台很贵的机器。

sentences.en: Did he design the chip or he just built, it was just like a...
sentences.zh: 那是他自己设计的芯片，还是说他只是造了，就像一个……

sentences.en: It was a combination of, uh, doing the chip design because it was, uh, the processor on it basically executed the byte code coming out of the Modula 2 compiler directly.
sentences.zh: 这是结合了芯片设计，因为它的处理器基本上是直接执行来自 Modula 2 编译器的字节码。

sentences.en: And so, so it had its, its own, its own custom CPU, its own custom hardware.
sentences.zh: 所以，它有它自己的、专属的 CPU，有它自己的专属硬件。

sentences.en: It had a portrait display.
sentences.zh: 它有一个纵向显示器（portrait display）。

sentences.en: It had its own Modula 2 based operating system, kind of a, a window based, based operating system.
sentences.zh: 它有自己的基于 Modula 2 的操作系统，算是一种基于窗口的操作系统。

sentences.en: Quite an impressive feat at the time.
sentences.zh: 在当时可以说是相当了不起的成就。

sentences.en: You can, you can look up, you can probably find emulators someplace to run, run a Lilith.
sentences.zh: 你可以，你可以去查查，大概还能在某些地方找到模拟器来运行 Lilith。

sentences.en: So, you know, at the time it's, you know, I salivated over these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在那个年代，这东西，你知道的让我垂涎三尺。

sentences.en: It was like, oh, I really want a Lilith computer, but no possible way that I could afford one.
sentences.zh: 当时就觉得，天哪，我太想要一台 Lilith 计算机了，但根本不可能买得起。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: You basically need to be, you know, in research at a university with some kind of government funding to, to get a Lilith.
sentences.zh: 你基本上得是，你知道的，在大学里搞研究，还得有某种政府资助，才能弄到一台 Lilith。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it was, you know, one of those, those dead ends in the, uh, in the evolution of, of, of hardware and software.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，它你知道的，是软硬件演进过程中的那些死胡同之一。

sentences.en: But it's, it's an interesting era because these days you could not, I think, create a, uh, create your own machine at the same scale.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个有趣的时代，因为如今你不可能，我觉得，再按同样的规模创造一台，创造属于你自己的机器了。

sentences.en: You need to be...
sentences.zh: 你必须得……

sentences.en: A lot of people kind of do now with FPGAs.
sentences.zh: 现在很多人借助 FPGA 其实在这么做。

sentences.en: So, so, you know, I, I kind of think you could these days with, uh, you, you could basically build your own processor FPGAs and build custom ASICs.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，你知道的，我觉得现在的确可以，呃，你基本上可以用 FPGA 构建自己的处理器，并制造自定义 ASIC。

sentences.en: The only place where I see people doing that is kind of emulating old game hardware.
sentences.zh: 我唯一看到有人在这么做的领域，也就是模拟一下老旧的游戏硬件。

sentences.en: But you, you don't think that, uh, that, that era in the past was a golden era of hardware and software design and that we're now in a much more homogenized, um,
sentences.zh: 但难道你不认为，呃，过去那个时代是软硬件设计的黄金时代，而我们现在正身处一个高度同质化的，呃，

sentences.en: era and an era where, um, the, certainly the high end of chips is, um, only for, or only the high end, or let me put it in a minute.
sentences.zh: 时代，在这个时代里，呃，高端芯片无疑是，呃，或者说只有高端芯片——让我换个说法。

sentences.en: The high end of computers today, um, uh, and I don't mean, like, the most powerful computers, but, like, you know, the best computers, you know, the, the,
sentences.zh: 今天的高端电脑，呃，呃——我指的不是那种最强大的电脑，而是那种，你知道的，最好的电脑，你知道的，那些，

sentences.en: the computers in your phone that are in your laptop, you know, something like the Nintendo Switch, um, those are produced by gigantic corporations and have huge,
sentences.zh: 装在你手机里、笔记本电脑里的电脑，或者像任天堂 Switch 那样的设备，呃，它们都是由巨型公司制造的，背后有巨大，

sentences.en: huge amounts of investment, um, to go into them, um, to produce them.
sentences.zh: 巨大的资金投入，呃，用来研发和生产它们。

sentences.en: Whereas, you know, back in the, the 70s and the 80s, um, you could, uh, you, you could create a, a thing that was a good thing at a much smaller, a much smaller scale,
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道的，回到 70 和 80 年代，呃，你完全可以，呃，以小得多的规模，小得多的体量，打造出一个好东西，

sentences.en: not quite maybe in, in your, your garage, but certainly close.
sentences.zh: 虽然可能不完全是在你的车库里，但也绝对差不离了。

sentences.en: It's interesting that, you know, I don't think, well, it's somewhat the same as like, you know, Steve and Steve, right, created the, the Apple one, you know,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，你知道的，我觉得，这其实有点像，你知道的，两个史蒂夫（Steve and Steve），对吧，他们在车库里打造了，

sentences.en: famously in the garage.
sentences.zh: 著名的 Apple One。

sentences.en: And, uh, you know, did the work for the Apple two as well, um, uh, very small scale.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，你知道的，他们也为 Apple Two 做出了工作，呃，规模非常小。

sentences.en: And there's no way that you would do that today and compete with, with a Mac or a windows box.
sentences.zh: 而现在你绝对不可能再这样做，还能去跟 Mac 或 Windows 电脑竞争。

sentences.en: There's just no way, but at the same time for them, they were creating something that ultimately would compete with, you know, uh, minis and mainframes.
sentences.zh: 根本没有可能，但与此同时，对他们来说，他们当时创造的东西最终将能够与，你知道的，小型机和大型机竞争。

sentences.en: And there was no way for them to directly compete with that.
sentences.zh: 而当时他们根本没有办法与那些东西直接竞争。

sentences.en: And surprisingly, the barrier to do, like, small entry-level hardware these days is really low.
sentences.zh: 出人意料的是，如今做这种小型入门级硬件的门槛其实非常低。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look, uh, small startups like, uh, uh, uh, tilt five, which just does, does, uh, you know, an amazing setup for, for, uh, kind of augmented reality for, uh,
sentences.zh: 我是说，你看，呃，像 Tilt 5 这样的小型初创公司，它们刚刚做了，呃，你知道的，为，呃，

sentences.en: board games, which is, is very cool.
sentences.zh: 桌游打造的非常惊艳的增强现实（AR）设置，这真的很酷。

sentences.en: And so it's little Pico projectors in glasses, uh, uh, Jerry Ellsworth's work, absolutely brilliant hardware.
sentences.zh: 所以它就是眼镜里的小型微微型投影仪（Pico projectors），呃，这是杰瑞·埃尔斯沃斯（Jerry Ellsworth）的工作，绝对是天才般的硬件。

sentences.en: And it's basically, you know, one woman, a small company, a small team who's, who's, who's doing, uh, this, this relatively inexpensive custom hardware.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是，你知道的，一个女性、一家小公司、一个小团队，在做，在做，呃，这种相对便宜的定制硬件。

sentences.en: I guess you have a, I guess you have a fair point.
sentences.zh: 我想你说的，我想你确实有道理。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, and you see like one-off little consumer products all over the place.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，到处都能看到各种独立的小众消费级产品。

sentences.en: Will somebody build an entry-level laptop or OS or something that eventually displaces Mac and Windows?
sentences.zh: 会不会有人造出一款入门级的笔记本电脑、操作系统或者别的什么，最终取代 Mac 和 Windows 呢？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe, you know, I think it's, it's doable.
sentences.zh: 也许吧，你知道，我觉得这并非不可能。

sentences.en: Um, really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Uh, it's just, you're not going to start with a head-on attack.
sentences.zh: 呃，只是你不会一开始就选择正面进攻。

sentences.en: You're going to start building, building something that, that Apple and Microsoft view as a, as a non-threat toy in the same way that, that deck viewed the Apple II as, as a toy.
sentences.zh: 你会先打造出一些被苹果和微软视为“无威胁的玩具”的东西，就像当年 DEC 把 Apple II 看作是一个玩具一样。

sentences.en: You know, not anything that would be at all competitive with them ever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，压根没觉得它会对他们构成任何竞争威胁。

sentences.en: Have you, have you tried this?
sentences.zh: 你试过这个吗？

sentences.en: I, cause I had never heard of tilt five.
sentences.zh: 因为我从来没听说过 Tilt 5。

sentences.en: And when you mentioned AR board games, I have always thought that, uh, I've only ever done one D&D campaign,
sentences.zh: 当你提到 AR 桌游时，我一直在想，呃，我这辈子只玩过一次 D&D 战役，

sentences.en: Dungeons and Dragons for the 1% of our audience that doesn't know what that refers to.
sentences.zh: 也就是《龙与地下城》（Dungeons and Dragons），为了我们那 1% 不知道这是什么意思的听众解释一下。

sentences.en: And, uh, it was cool, but it was done virtually during the pandemic with my siblings and siblings' partners.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，这很酷，但那是在疫情期间通过虚拟方式跟我兄弟姐妹以及他们伴侣一起玩的。

sentences.en: And it was, uh, very cool, but it was done through like a 2D online, you know, like you're going through the board and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 虽然，呃，非常酷，但它是通过那种 2D 的在线方式，你知道的，就像在棋盘上移动看风景之类的。

sentences.en: And it's, I think you get a lot more out of having like a real board or if you go to a game store and you have one of those sort of like, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，如果你有一个真实的棋盘，或者如果你去游戏店，看到那种，你知道的，

sentences.en: uh,
sentences.zh: 呃，

sentences.en: not battlefields or whatever.
sentences.zh: 不是战场那种东西，体验会丰富得多。

sentences.en: Have you, have you, have you ever played D&D at a, at a game store?
sentences.zh: 你，你，你有没有在游戏店里玩过 D&D？

sentences.en: No, but I have been to, uh, game stores.
sentences.zh: 没有，但我去过，呃，游戏店。

sentences.en: Trust me, having the online thing to like keep track of all the state is actually very convenient.
sentences.zh: 相信我，有个在线工具来追踪所有的状态其实非常方便。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, my point, my point being though, is regardless of if you're doing it in person with a dungeon master that is expert at, you know, moving things around,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我的意思是，不管你是跟一个擅长移动棋盘物件、

sentences.en: making spatially aware stuff, or you're doing it on this 2D thing.
sentences.zh: 具备空间感知能力的地下城主（DM）进行面对面游戏，还是在用这个 2D 东西玩，

sentences.en: The real like first, like, you know, world-class experience that you want is this kind of AR thing where the, the dungeon master has, you know, ahead of the campaign, gone forward,
sentences.zh: 真正的那种首屈一指的、世界级的体验，其实是你想要的这种 AR 形式：地下城主在战役开始前，就已经提前准备好了，

sentences.en: set this up of the different corners that you, the different directions you could go.
sentences.zh: 把你们可能前往的不同方向、不同的角落都设置好。

sentences.en: And as the campaign unfolds, you're just like, you don't have to like, oh, the mist comes over, you know, sure.
sentences.zh: 随着战役的展开，你甚至不需要——哦，大雾弥漫过来，当然，

sentences.en: The, the dungeon master can narrate that, but you know, with the swoosh of a hand, you know, the mist actually like appears on this and you could do it virtually.
sentences.zh: 地下城主可以旁白解说，但你知道的，只要手轻轻一挥，大雾就真的会在这上面显现出来，而且你可以虚拟地做到这一点。

sentences.en: Everyone has a set of glasses, you know, they're just staring at whatever table.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有一副眼镜，你知道的，大家就盯着随便什么桌子就行。

sentences.en: And so I want to use my imagination.
sentences.zh: 所以我还是想用自己的想象力。

sentences.en: It's like reading the books, like, you know, movies are nice, but sometimes one wants to read a book.
sentences.zh: 就像读书一样，你知道的，电影虽好，但有时候人就是想读本书。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Bryce is not invited to the future Dungeons and Dragons campaign that I will have using this Tilt 5 technology.
sentences.zh: 布莱斯（Bryce）没有被邀请参加我将来要用这个 Tilt 5 技术举办的《龙与地下城》战役。

sentences.en: But I, I went to this site and as soon as you said that, I was like, wait, is there a company that already has the hardware to do this?
sentences.zh: 但我，我去了他们的网站，你刚一说完，我就在想，等等，难道已经有一家公司拥有做这件事的硬件了吗？

sentences.en: And sure enough, they've got like a little, a demo of, it doesn't show a D&D campaign,
sentences.zh: 果不其然，他们有一个小小的演示，虽然没有展示 D&D 战役，

sentences.en: but exactly this kind of thing where everyone's got a little controller and they're playing these little fun games.
sentences.zh: 但确确实实就是这种每个人都有一个小控制器、在玩这些有趣的小游戏的场景。

sentences.en: Anyways, this is a long winded of like, this is something that's been in the back of my head of like the, this future technology would be awesome.
sentences.zh: 总之，我兜了这么大一个圈子，其实就是想说，这种未来科技太棒了，这想法一直盘旋在我的脑海里。

sentences.en: Have you used this?
sentences.zh: 你用过这个吗？

sentences.en: And do you know if like, it's actually at the state where you can do this kind of stuff?
sentences.zh: 你知道它现在是不是真的已经发展到能做到这种程度的阶段了？

sentences.en: Oh yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: So, so this is, the Tilt 5 stuff is actually Jerry's, you know, second generation.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以这个，Tilt 5 的产品实际上已经是杰瑞的第二代了。
